scenes.vo: The biggest crypto hack on record started with a fake job interview. Here's what changed.
Binance's incident report says attackers posed as executives, sent an engineer a coding test hiding malware, then used an internal AI tool to reach two wallet engineers.
Here's why traders are watching it. Binance says about two point eight five billion dollars is frozen, and it replenished most affected tokens with company funds.
The catch. The FBI blames North Korean hackers, and more than three billion dollars is still out there. The same fake recruiter trick targets regular people too.
Here's what happens next. Watch how much more gets frozen, and whether other exchanges tighten access to signing systems and internal AI tools.
